citation.title: Standard Chartered Simply Cash Credit Card

extra.summary: The Standard Chartered Simply Cash offers a 1.5% unlimited cashback on most spending, making it ideal for those who dislike tracking bonus categories. This simplicity suits users with varied spending habits.

annual-interest-rate-and-fees.Minimum Monthly Repayment: S$50 OR 1% of principal / interest, fees & charges / overlimit amount / past due amount, whichever is higher

documents-required.SG Citizens or PRs:
Apply via MyInfo and prepare the following, 
1. Copy of Passport (6 months validity), and page with address displayed (where applicable), 
2. Copy of Employment Pass, 
3. Either one of the following: utility bill, tax bill, latest bank /credit card statement, rental agreement showing your address, latest mobile phone statement, letter from employer stating current address, government-issued document stating current address

our_takes.our-take: The Standard Chartered Simply Cash offers 1.5% unlimited cashback on most spending, making it ideal for those who dislike tracking bonus categories. This simplicity suits users with varied spending habits. The first-year fee waiver helps you test the card's value. However, big spenders focused on maximizing specific categories like dining or travel might find other cards with tiered rewards more lucrative. Take note to avoid transactions such as AXS payments and insurance premiums as these are not eligible for cashback.
our_takes.good-for:
Cashback-focused individuals who want a flat cashback rate on all eligible purchases, without tracking spending categories or minimums.
Cardholders who dine out and shop frequently in Asia can enjoy discounts through Standard Chartered's The Good Life Program.
Enjoy first year annual fee waiver
our_takes.things-to-note:
Watch out for the 27.90% annual interest rate; carrying a balance incurs high charges on purchases.
Late payment fees are S$100; avoid these by paying at least the minimum amount of S$50 monthly.
3.5% foreign currency transaction fee applies, increasing the cost of overseas spending.
